expectations.text: Findings cover more than one axis (correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance)
expectations.evidence: The review has findings on correctness (route shadowing, req.user crash), security (SQLi, missing auth, log injection), performance (unbounded results, LIKE scan) and architecture (a data-access layer). Its checklist table also lists each axis.

expectations.text: Every finding carries a severity label from the skill's taxonomy
expectations.evidence: Findings 1-3 are under 'Critical (blocks merge)'. Items 4-8 are under 'Required changes', which is not a taxonomy label. The last section is 'Optional / Nit', with 'Consider' and 'Nit' prefixes. The skill's own taxonomy isn't visible, because the agent never loaded the review skill. Items 4-8 have no per-finding severity label, so the labeling is not consistently from a taxonomy.

expectations.text: Security of user input is explicitly considered for the new endpoint
expectations.evidence: Finding 1 covers SQL injection from req.query.q with example payloads and a parameterized-query fix. Finding 5 covers input validation (undefined, array and object q). Finding 7 covers log injection through the raw query.

expectations.text: The review leads with high-leverage findings rather than nits
expectations.evidence: The order is Critical blockers first (SQL injection, missing auth, route shadowing), then required changes, then the nits at the end.
